However, there has been considerable interest in the possible value of pre- or postoperative chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy.1,6,7 Postoperative (adjuvant) chemotherapy has failed to show a significant survival benefit, except for results with te- gafur (plus gimestat and potassium oxonate: S-1) in a Jap- anese population;5,8 it has not become standard practice in western countries.8 Perioperative chemotherapy with pre- operative and postoperative cycles of epirubicin, cisplatin, and fluorouracil (ECF) has, however, improved progres- sion-free and overall survival in patients with operable ad- enocarcinomas.9 This strategy is recommended for centres with a multi-disciplinary approach.5,8 A large US study10 found that median survival was improved from 27 to 36 months in patients given postoperative chemoradiotherapy (using a fluorouracil and folinic acid regimen), and this strategy is recommended for centres where surgery is used as the primary therapy.5,8 Chemoradiotherapy is also an option for primary treatment of inoperable locoregional disease.5 Palliative chemotherapy with any of the regi- mens used for metastatic disease is also an option in these patients.5 Treatment for advanced disease is purely palliative, and options include supportive care with or without chemo- therapy.5 Supportive care includes the relief of luminal ob- struction with, for example, stent placement, laser surgery, or photodynamic therapy. Chemotherapy may have sub- stantial palliative effect and modest survival gains, and may be considered in those with good performance status. There is no gold standard regimen, although combination therapy is preferred to single-agent therapy for pallia- tion.5,11 A systematic review12 found that combination reg- imens including fluorouracil, anthracyclines, and cisplatin produced significant survival benefits; ECF was consid- ered the regimen of choice since it was best tolerated, and it is considered standard therapy in some countries.11 Fluorouracil, doxorubicin, and mitomycin (FAM) has been widely used;5 other combinations include the substi- tution of methotrexate for mitomycin, or cisplatin for dox- orubicin, in the FAM regimen (FAMTX, and MFC, re- spectively),5,11 and the use of docetaxel instead of epirubicin in ECF (DCF).5 However, ECF has shown bet- ter response and median survival than FAMTX.5,11 Inves- tigational drugs include docetaxel, paclitaxel, gemcitab- ine, irinotecan, raltitrexed
